new_row.notes: {"row_key": "S6_06_BLIND:P1.18", "night_checkpoint": "30", "source_file": "sources/newer_night/checkpoint30/S6_06_BLIND_results.csv", "where_proved": "notes/part1.tex", "source_statement": "In the algebraic splitting $\\sigma_b$, the function $h_b$ has its unique global minimum at the finite-root point $\\lambda=\\infty$. The minimum is the exact Frobenius period constant \\[ h_{b,\\min}=-\\frac{96}{625\\pi}\\operatorname{Re}(XH_\\infty)_{03}, \\qquad h_{b,\\min}=-1.0945402503114027801162682630549457037\\ldots, \\tag{1.18.1} \\] where $X$ is the normalized integral intertwiner of P1.15 and $H_\\infty$ is the regular infinity-root limit of its fundamental solution, normalized to be the identity at $\\lambda=1$ before multiplication by $X$. Formula (1.18.1), the rational connection, and those two normalizations specify the constant exactly. A certified enclosure has radius $4.04\\cdot10^{-56}$ about the 56-digit midpoint retained in \\path{code/part1/minimum_certificate_summary.json}. Consequently the exact domain of completed transverse periods is \\[ c>-h_{b,\\min},\\qquad \\operatorname{Im}\\xi>-h_{b,\\min} \\] for the real and complex parameters, respectively.
